The proposed answer is correct. I checked the argument but did not run any code.

**Structure.** A permutation of shape (n−m, m) or (n−m, 1^m) has a longest increasing subsequence of length n−m. Typically it is a unique "main" increasing chain plus m outliers. The number of choices of (P, V) is about C(n,m)². This matches the number of permutations of the target shape, (f^λ)², which is C(n,m)²(1−O(1/n)) for the two-row shape and C(n−1,m)² ~ C(n,m)² for the hook. So P and V are asymptotically independent uniform m-subsets.

**Fixed points.** The outliers contribute at most m fixed points, which is negligible against n. A main position i is fixed exactly when the number of elements of P below i equals the number of elements of V below i. At scaled position x, these counts are independent Bin(m, x) variables. The expected fixed-point proportion therefore tends to

∫₀¹ Σₖ C(m,k)² x^{2k}(1−x)^{2m−2k} dx.

**Integral.** Each term is a Beta integral, equal to C(m,k)²(2k)!(2m−2k)!/(2m+1)!. Rewriting C(m,k)²(2k)!(2m−2k)! as (m!)² C(2k,k) C(2m−2k, m−k) and using Σₖ C(2k,k) C(2m−2k, m−k) = 4^m gives 4^m (m!)²/(2m+1)!.

**Check for m = 1.** The formula gives 4/6 = 2/3, which matches the stated direct count for shape (n−1, 1).

VERDICT: ACCEPT
